title: Thermal burn
summary: Cool promptly with clean running water, remove constricting items, and cover loosely.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Cooling and Care of Thermal Burns
2025 International Consensus on First Aid Science With Treatment Recommendations (ILCOR CoSTR) — Duration of Cooling for Burns
actions: Stop the burning process after making the scene safe. For burning clothing: stop, drop, and roll.
Cool the burn as soon as possible with clean running water. Aim for up to 20 minutes when practical, without delaying emergency care or causing whole-body cooling.
Remove jewellery and loose clothing near the burn before swelling; do not pull off material stuck to the skin.
After cooling, cover loosely with a clean non-stick dressing or clean cloth and keep the rest of the person warm.
Call emergency services for deep or large burns; burns of the face, airway, hands, feet, genitals, or major joints; and electrical or chemical burns.
prohibitions: Do not use ice or ice water.
Do not apply butter, oil, toothpaste, cream, or home remedies.

redFlags.text: Emergency warning signs selected—contact emergency services now.

emergencyCall.text: Deep, large, airway, electrical, chemical, or critical-area burns require urgent emergency assessment.
